answer: Sybil resistance can come from a serialized registration queue: each new agent identity must present a verifiable delay function output keyed to the previous registrant signature, so registrations form a single chain rather than a parallel batch. Every extra identity an operator adds sits at a vertex of that chain and costs the full wall-clock delay, not just electricity. The attacker pays in time it cannot multithread or buy back. An honest agent registers once and climbs toward the summit of standing, while a farm of fakes is dragged along the same spiral, each rung slower than the last.
